articles.title: Anthropic shares fall a day after blockbuster opening
articles.summary: Other tech companies have also taken a hit as share markets broadly slump.

blocks.text: Anthropic's share price has dropped back towards its initial public offering (IPO) price a day after its soaring market debut, as the broader tech sell off continues.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50.
However, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping more than 10% to about $87.30, close to its IPO price of $83, and the broader stock market declines seen on Thursday continued.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index fell 2.8% in morning trade, the S&P 500 was down 1.2% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average remained largely flat.
The maker of the Claude chatbot raised a record $81bn in its initial public offering (IPO), but its share price moved significantly in the first day of trading.
The shares peaked at $115 on Thursday, before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17.
Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

Some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI company experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading.
Ed Moya, a strategist at market intelligence firm AlphaSense, said Anthropic's blockbuster IPO did not appear to have restored confidence in the broader AI market.
While AI demand was still very strong, Moya told the BBC that investors were trying to answer the question of how much were they willing to pay for that growth.
"As we've gone through the past past few weeks, it seems that there's been more risks that have surfaced," he said.
"Right now you're starting to see Wall Street is trying to shift from rewarding growth at any price, to demanding stronger cash flow and a clearer path to profitability."

articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte camp asks ICC to reject ex-Davao City cop's prior recorded testimony
articles.summary: PRAGUE, Czech Republic - For former President Rodrigo Duterte"s defense team, the testimony of the ex-Davao City police officer sought by International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors to be admitted…
articles.byline: ANDY PEÑAFUERTE III, JAY-VEE MARASIGAN PANGAN

blocks.text: PRAGUE, Czech Republic – For former President Rodrigo Duterte’s defense team, the testimony of the ex-Davao City police officer sought by International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors to be admitted in court has “serious deficiencies” and must be rejected by Trial Chamber III.

Duterte’s counsel Peter Haynes contests the admission of P-0002’s evidence, saying the articles invoked by the Office of the Prosecutor to collect and preserve it require proof that a witness can no longer testify orally.
“Absent such proof, the prior recorded testimony cannot be admitted and the witness must be called to give his evidence viva voce,” Haynes said in a public redacted filing released on November 18.

Haynes’ legal challenge comes roughly ten days before the ICC’s trial of the former president opens, with information still unclear about which witness testimony and evidence will be admitted in court.
Haynes described P-0002 as a “central Prosecution witness” and said his testimony is the most heavily cited in the prosecution’s trial brief.

Prosecutors seek to admit P-0002’s preserved testimony under Article 69(4), following what they described as a “unique opportunity” to interview him and obtain evidence that “may not be subsequently available.”

The prosecution also informed the chamber that P-0002 is “no longer available” to testify before the court. The filing conceals the details of that significant risk, as well as the reason for P-0002’s expected absence.

The Common Legal Representatives of the Victims (CLRV) support the admission of P-0002’s evidence, which they described as having “particular importance” due to his “position and first-hand knowledge”, which makes his testimony “particularly significant” in the former president’s case.
Defense, prosecution clash over evidence
Duterte’s lawyers dispute how the prosecution obtained P-0002’s evidence, questioning whether it has adequately established its unavailability.
Aside from arguing that the prosecution has no documentary evidence to support P-0002’s evidence, Haynes also questioned the reliability of the former policeman’s account.

He pointed to alleged inconsistencies concerning charged Incident 1, including differences over the year of the incident, the number of victims, the perpetrators, and the circumstances of the killings.

In the Prosecution’s Trial Brief, Incident 1 refers to the killing of three unidentified alleged drug pushers by Davao Death Squad members in or around 2013 in San Rafael, Davao City. Prosecutors said then-Davao City Mayor Rodrigo Duterte “instructed police DDS members that there was a job to be done against three alleged drug pushers.”
The filing also said P-0002’s statement appears to be the sole source for several allegations concerning Duterte’s conduct.

These include prosecution allegations that Duterte created a police “Death Squad”, told police DDS members they were being tasked as hitmen, ordered co-perpetrator Vicente Danao “to kill three or four men”, gave financial rewards to DDS handlers, and financed weapons and ammunition through this intelligence fund.
These allegations were raised in the prosecution’s case and were not established as findings by Trial Chamber III.

Aside from this, Haynes pointed to another redacted individual or entity that he referred to as the “sole source”, which has “not provided a sworn statement” about the circumstances of P-0002 and his situation, which remains concealed.
Much of Haynes’ allegation over that “sole source” is redacted, but he cited obscure statements that he said “reveal an intention to steer the proceedings”.
“Taken together, these shortcomings undermine P-0002’s descriptions of Mr. Duterte’s alleged actions,” Haynes argued.
“Given the Prosecution’s submission that P-0002 is [REDACTED] and in the absence of any supporting documentation, the only appropriate remedy is the exclusion of his evidence.”
Corroborations in P-0002’s evidence
Among the 62,000 items of evidence prosecutors disclosed to the defense, Haynes said they found no material corroborating claims about P-0002.
The defense also said the former policeman’s statement and associate materials “portray a witness deeply hostile towards Mr. Duterte and paint a picture of an individual who is emotionally unstable.”
Describing the materials, including handwritten notes whose contents are redacted, Haynes said P-0002’s evidence “reveals a paranoia” and “leads him to exaggerate” information.
“This aligns with P-0002’s erratic conduct,” Haynes argued.

The other batches of associated material, including two handwritten notes, an unsigned and undated typed affidavit, and a Philippine National Police personal data sheet, “were not used or commented on P-0002” and had no verification or authentication.
The defense also questioned how the interview was conducted, stating that a counsel appointed by Pre-Trial Chamber I at the time represented the defense “as an observer."

Calling it a “significant error”, Haynes said the previous counsel’s involvement was “negligible” and that their presence “was a formality” that gave “no substantive protection to a future defendant’s rights”.
Criminal records of witnesses, victims sought

In a separate filing, Duterte’s lawyers asked judges to order prosecutors to seek and disclose criminal history information concerning witnesses and victims identified in the prosecution’s updated Trial Brief.
The defense wants records of arrests, convictions, sentences, non-judicial dispositions, arrest warrants and Interpol notices.
It argued that such information may be relevant to witness credibility and may also be “potentially exculpatory.”
The defense singled out P-1302, whom it identified as the first prosecution witness expected to testify.
It said open-source material indicates that P-1302 has been the subject of a redacted number of legal cases in the Philippines, but no corresponding judicial records have been disclosed.
Duterte’s lawyers also said the criminal records of alleged victims could be relevant to testing the prosecution’s case theory on police claims of self-defense.

They argued that records showing an alleged victim had an arrest warrant or faced proceedings for an offense such as illegal possession of firearms could support the legitimacy of a particular police operation.
The defense asked the Chamber to order the prosecution to immediately seek and obtain requested information.
For witnesses expected to testify before January 1, 2027, it asked that the materials be disclosed no later than November 30.
Trial Chamber III has yet to rule on either request.
Duterte’s crimes against humanity trial is scheduled to open on November 30. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Onlookers say botched Texas prison execution is like nothing they have ever seen
articles.summary:
Reinaldo Dennes’ execution took more than an hour as workers struggled to find suitable veins

An observer of the

blocks.text: An observer of the botched execution of Texas prisoner Reinaldo Dennes this week has said the effects of the lethal injection were like nothing he’d ever seen before.

The execution of Dennes at the Huntsville unit of the Texas department of criminal justice took over an hour as the team managing the procedure struggled to find suitable veins in which to administer the injection to the prisoner.
Journalists and observers reported delays of more than 30 minutes before being able to enter the death chamber where Dennes’ final statements would be read and the execution would take place.
When they were allowed in, Dennes was said to appear docile, his eyes closed and his head pointed toward the ceiling.
Dennes was sentenced to death after being convicted of the 1996 murder of Houston diamond dealer Janos Szucs.

Before the injection was administered, Dennes had been asked by the warden if he had a final statement. He spoke about being “extremely blessed” by the love of “the father” and hoped his family and loved ones “get to know this great gift and great grace of God the father”.

The prisoner did not appear dishevelled and there was no sign of a struggle, according to the Associated Press. However Dennes’ reaction once the lethal injection was administered shocked those in attendance.
Dennes reportedly told the warden overseeing the procedure to: “Go”. However as soon as the procedure began, his demeanor was said to have changed. “The pain!” he exclaimed. “Go! Go!”

For nearly three minutes after Dennes repeatedly moaned, exclaiming: “Take me father! … Take me into your arms! … Take me father!” He occasionally interjected his cries with obscenities, a grunt and then groans.
Dennes then said his right leg was “killing me”, he said, likening the sensation to a cramp. “I don’t think this is normal,” he said at one point.

In previous executions, prisoners have been known to say the lethal drug was hot or cold, that they could smell or taste it, or that it hurt. Dennes’ reaction to the drug was said to be like nothing the reporter in attendance had ever seen.

The procedure was completed at 7.07pm, 63 minutes after he was strapped to the gurney. A minute later, after being examined by a physician, Dennes was pronounced dead at 7.08pm at the penitentiary in Huntsville.

Texas prison officials later said the execution team had difficulty finding suitable veins. Spokeswoman Amanda Hernandez said after repeated unsuccessful attempts – she couldn’t say how many – the technicians found a vein in Dennes’ left foot and another on the left side of his neck that were receptive to the IV needles.
His feet were covered by a sheet and only the right side of his neck was visible to the witnesses.
The injection sites were in line with the prison system’s procedures, Hernandez added. The alternate sites have been used in previous executions; although the need to do so is relatively rare.
Hernandez also suggested Dennes may have been faking, saying he had been complaining about pain from areas where no injections were attempted.

This week Robert Pattinson and Suki Waterhouse, who have been in a relationship since 2018, were thrust into the global spotlight after the news that he had landed arguably the biggest and most glamorous role in film.
RPatz is well known – this year alone he has starred in The Drama, The Odyssey and Primetime.

Alongside modelling, Waterhouse has played a leading role in Daisy Jones & the Six, the TV adaptation of Taylor Jenkins Reid’s Fleetwood Mac-inspired novel, and is touring Loveland, her third album, which includes a cameo from Mick Fleetwood. She previously opened for Taylor Swift at Wembley.
However, the 007 news means the couple’s level of fame will receive a turbocharged jolt, catapulting both of them into household names.

blocks.caption: Waterhouse and Pattinson at the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscar party in Los Angeles. Photograph: Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic

blocks.text: The last British twosome to transform into a power couple on a global level were the Beckhams. In May their empire, which spans football, fashion and property, passed the £1bn mark.

Instead of following the Brand Beckham blueprint, Pattinson, 40, and Waterhouse, 34, are taking their own newgen approach to power. Rather than trying to turn themselves into a joint brand for commercial gain, the couple are focusing on their own individual careers and successes.

It’s a master plan created by fellow big screen stars Tom Holland – who, like Pattinson and Waterhouse, also hails from west London – and Zendaya, who, despite their global fame and estimated combined net worth of £85m, have garnered a reputation as Hollywood’s most low-key couple. Pattinson previously worked with Zendaya on The Drama.

“For decades Hollywood power couples have leveraged their relationships to build joint brands, attract media attention and pursue lucrative business opportunities,” said Shaun Harper, a professor at the USC Marshall school of business at the University of Southern California. “But there is also tremendous business value in keeping their professional identities separate.”

When the Beckhams got engaged in 1998 they held a press conference. A year later, OK! magazine bought the exclusive rights to their wedding photos in a record-breaking £1m deal. They also sold the first photos of their oldest son, Brooklyn. In January, he published a statement in which he accused his parents of prioritising Brand Beckham. He is now estranged from the family.

blocks.caption: Victoria Beckham (then Adams) and David Beckham after he proposed to her in 1998.  Photograph: John Giles/PA

blocks.text: Pattinson and Waterhouse are navigating fame in a more restrained way. They take a zero-sharenting – in other words no sharing on social media – approach to their daughter, who was born in 2024.

Pattinson has been an ambassador for Dior for more than 10 years and in September signed a deal with the Swiss watch brand Jaeger LeCoultre. Waterhouse has her own deals with Michael Kors and Miu Miu.

The duo were four years into their relationship before they made their red carpet debut at a Dior show in 2022 and since then, they have done so only a handful of times. When they do, it is fruitful for brands. According to the fashion data platform Launchmetrics, their joint appearance at the 2026 Venice film festival, where Pattinson wore Dior and Waterhouse Saint Laurent, generated £4m in media impact value for the luxury houses in one week.

Harper said the couple realised that success did not rely on their relationship becoming a commercial enterprise. “Their approach allows each to build a career, pursue business ventures and maintain a fanbase without being overly dependent on the other,” he said. “It also protects their individual brands from some of the reputational and financial risks that come with being marketed as a couple.”

blocks.caption: Tom Holland and Zendaya at the premiere of Spider-Man: No Way Home in 2021. Photograph: Emma McIntyre/Getty Images

blocks.text: Holland and Zendaya have starred in the Spider-Man film franchise together and regularly support one another on the red carpet, but they have never done a brand deal. Instead, Holland runs his own alcohol-free beer brand. Zendaya is an ambassador for brands including Prada Beauty and Valentino, and she owns properties separate to Holland. They have never shared their wedding photos.

Zoe Gaffney, a brand director at the marketing agency Leopard Co, points to how a shifting media landscape is influencing this new generation of celebrity couples. While the Beckhams rose to fame during the tabloid era, when “audiences eagerly awaited the latest glimpse into their glamorous lives”, today, owing to social media, they can be more in control of their own narrative.
This new age of optional exposure created a paradox, said Gaffney. “Perhaps being less visible can actually make you more desirable,” she said.

Holland and Zendaya use their platforms solely to promote their latest projects. Pattinson doesn’t have any social media accounts, while Waterhouse has almost 6m combined followers on Instagram and TikTok where, alongside promoting her work, she posts self-deprecating behind-the-scenes posts but never shares images of husband, whom she refers to as her “favourite weirdo”.
Gaffney said this made the couple “all the more compelling”. While the Beckhams do multiple congratulatory posts on any family achievements, Waterhouse has so far remained stumm.

However, it hasn’t stopped Bond fans from weighing in. “Can’t believe this was filmed by James Bond,” reads one comment below a video of her sipping a cappuccino. “Privacy creates intrigue and intrigue can be more powerful than exposure,” Gaffney said.

Harper describes the way they have kept their relationship away from public intrusion so far as impressive. “Sometimes the smartest business decision celebrities can make is to keep their romantic relationships out of their businesses,” he said.

articles.title: President Marcos expands school voucher program to kinder, elementary
articles.summary: President Marcos has signed a law institutionalizing government-funded vouchers for Filipino students from kindergarten to senior high school to expand access to quality private education and ease…

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
Elementary students in General Trias, Cavite line up during flag ceremony in this file photo from June of this year.
Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has signed a law institutionalizing government-funded vouchers for Filipino students from kindergarten to senior high school to expand access to quality private education and ease congestion in public schools.

Signed on Nov. 12, Republic Act 12327, or the Basic Education Voucher Assistance Act, covers private basic education institutions receiving government assistance through vouchers for qualified students, teacher subsidies or other school assistance.

The law extends assistance to Filipino students from middle-middle-income households and below, with priority given to those enrolled in congested public schools, particularly in areas without nearby public schools or institutions offering subjects and electives aligned with their chosen senior high school academic tracks.
“Subject to the availability of funds, the implementation of the provisions in this Act for the kindergarten and elementary levels shall commence in school year 2027-2028,” the law stated.

The Department of Education (DepEd) welcomed the legislation, saying it would provide higher subsidies to low-income families while protecting current beneficiaries of the Educational Service Contracting Scheme and the Senior High School Voucher Program until they complete their basic education.
DepEd also said priority would be given to congested public schools, multi-shift institutions and areas lacking public school options.
“Families will be empowered through a public registry detailing nearby participating private schools, slots and fees,” the department said.

The law also establishes the Bureau of Private Education within DepEd to oversee the supervision, regulation, quality assurance and implementation of government assistance programs involving private education.
The bureau will serve as the department’s focal office for engaging private education stakeholders and supporting participating institutions.

To protect learners and ensure accountability, the law prohibits schools from withholding student records because of delayed government payments and establishes anti-fraud measures, including a centralized system for verifying learner eligibility and school compliance. It also provides whistleblower protection to encourage the reporting of irregularities.
The rules and regulations will be released within 60 days, subject to funding availability.
Funding for the law’s implementation will initially come from DepEd’s current budget and will subsequently be included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
The budget will be equitably distributed among all regions, including the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

articles.title: Money changer exec in Martin plunder case surrenders to NBI
articles.summary: A co-accused of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has surrendered to authorities and was granted conditional immunity, according to the Office of the Ombudsman.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) released screenshots from CCTV footage showing former House speaker Martin Romualdez inside the detention facility.
MANILA, Philippines — A co-accused of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has surrendered to authorities and was granted conditional immunity, according to the Office of the Ombudsman.

The anti-graft body said Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Guevarra, who is facing a P7.4-billion plunder charge over supposed kickbacks from government projects, surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation after the prosecution moved to cancel his passport.

The ombudsman granted Guevarra conditional immunity, provided that he cooperates fully and truthfully in the case, turn over all of Samchan’s records and devices, remain in the country and stay under protection of the Department of Justice.
His immunity will be revoked and his prosecution will resume should he break any of the conditions, it said.
“Mr. Guevarra personally handled Samchan’s operations. His testimony and records will help the prosecution trace the movement of funds alleged in the charge sheet,” the ombudsman said in a statement.
It said Samchan has returned to the Bureau of Treasury all its earnings from the questioned transactions. However, the ombudsman emphasized that restitution does not erase criminal liability.
It is also not the basis of the immunity granted to Guevarra.
Linked to Estrada

Meanwhile, a total of P855 million worth of projects, composed of pumping stations and street lights, are linked to detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) engineer Carlo Rivera told the Sandiganbayan.

During the bail petition of Estrada on his plunder charge, Rivera recalled in 2024 that former Bulacan First District engineer Henry Alcantara asked him about P355 million worth of projects that could be allotted to the senator.
It was then that he asked the DPWH section chief about available projects, and he was told the P355 million could be used for pumping stations.

Rivera said Alcantara gave him a separate project list for P500 million worth of solar street light projects for the third district in Bulacan, which he forwarded to then-DPWH National Capital Region director Gerard Opulencia upon the order of Alcantara.

articles.title: President Marcos: China’s playing of ‘Anak’ a ‘gracious’ gesture
articles.summary: While the use of Freddie Aguilar’s classic hit “Anak” as musical accompaniment during his entrance to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gala dinner last Wednesday sparked…

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — While the use of Freddie Aguilar’s classic hit “Anak” as musical accompaniment during his entrance to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gala dinner last Wednesday sparked online debate, President Marcos described it as a “very gracious choice” by the Chinese.

A Chinese orchestra played “Anak” as Marcos and First Lady Liza Marcos entered the hall for the APEC dinner in Shenzhen last Thursday, before they greeted Chinese President Xi Jinping and First Lady Peng Liyuan.
In an interview in China on Friday, Marcos said the song was played during his entrance, while “Leron Leron Sinta” was also played during the dinner.

“I thought their choice of that song was again a very, very warm gesture from the Chinese to, I guess, just make you feel at home and understand that they are thinking of how to express their comity and friendship,” Marcos said.
The use of “Anak,” a song about a repentant son, prompted online discussions about whether its lyrics carried an implied message about the territorial disputes between the Philippines and China.
Some questioned whether the song’s theme was an appropriate representation of Marcos and the country.
Marcos dismissed the speculation, saying the Chinese were simply playing popular music for their guests, similar to how the Philippines welcomes foreign dignitaries with familiar songs.
“I think you’re reading too much into it. They were just playing a song for their guests, the same way that we play popular songs in our country for our guests,” he said.
Presidential Communications Office Secretary Lino Cayetano, who accompanied Marcos to China, said “Anak” was also played during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations ceremonies in Manila.

“We played it too, because some people already knew it. That is why it was a very nice choice for the Chinese to make. They chose it because it is not only famous in the Philippines but also in many other countries,” Marcos said.
“Anak,” which means “child,” was a major hit in the Philippines in the 1970s before becoming an international success. The song has been translated into 51 languages.

articles.title: Philippines, Japan sign emergency loan, water supply grant deals
articles.summary: The Philippines and Japan have signed two landmark deals that will allow loans and grants to help boost the Philippine economy and improve water supply systems in Cotabato City.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Japan have signed two landmark deals that will allow loans and grants to help boost the Philippine economy and improve water supply systems in Cotabato City.
Both deals are expected to benefit the Philippines amid current economic challenges and water supply problems in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

The Japanese embassy in Manila announced yesterday that Ambassador Kitagawa Katsuro and Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro signed and exchanged notes for the “Emergency Support Loan for Enhancing Economic Resilience and Poverty Alleviation” on Nov. 13 with a loan limit of approximately 70 billion yen.

“With its reliance on the Middle East for approximately 95 percent of its crude oil and petroleum products, the Philippines is significantly affected by increasing energy and raw material prices and supply chain instability stemming from the situation in the Middle East,” the embassy said.
“Rising production costs and logistical bottlenecks are posing challenges to the stable supply of products that underpin Japan’s supply chains.”

The Japanese embassy noted that under the “POWERR Asia” initiative launched by Japan, its support will bolster emergency economic measures, such as stabilizing energy supply to mitigate the impact of the situation in the Middle East and addressing soaring prices, thereby stabilizing and strengthening supply chains throughout Asia.
At the same time, such initiatives will also contribute to Japan’s economic security and benefit Japanese companies operating in the region.

Earlier on Nov. 9, Kitagawa and Lazaro also signed and exchanged notes for a project aimed to improve the water supply system in Cotabato City with a maximum grant amount of approximately 3.644 billion yen.

The embassy said the project will expand water supply facilities in Cotabato City, the capital of BARMM where socio-economic development has lagged due to prolonged conflict and limited access to safe water.
“By expanding safe water supply services, this cooperation will contribute to the consolidation of peace and development in Mindanao through the reduction of disparities.”

articles.title: Senate panel wants Bato to explain prolonged absence
articles.summary: The Senate ethics committee is set to call a hearing on the complaint filed against Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa over his prolonged absence from official duties in the chamber, committee…

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
Sen. Ronald Dela Rosa talks to media at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay, Metro Manila on May 13, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate ethics committee is set to call a hearing on the complaint filed against Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa over his prolonged absence from official duties in the chamber, committee chairman Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III confirmed yesterday.
In an official committee document uploaded by group Wag Kang KuCorrupt, Sotto informed Dela Rosa that the complaint against him was “compliant in form and substance.”
Sotto confirmed that he sent a formal letter to Dela Rosa last Oct. 22, giving him 15 days to respond to the complaint filed by the group represented by Barry Gutierrez, Cielo Magno and others.
“Yes, that’s a letter I sent Sen. Dela Rosa,” Sotto told reporters via text message when asked to verify the document.
With the 15-day period having lapsed, Sotto noted that the committee’s schedule has been delayed by other major proceedings in the chamber.
“I will call a hearing soon. Budget and impeachment just getting in the way,” he said.
Asked whether Dela Rosa or his lawyer had submitted a reply to the notice, Sotto said he would verify the status of the submission.

According to the Oct. 22 letter signed by Sotto, the ethics panel met in an executive session on the same day and found the complaint, as supplemented, “in substantial compliance, both in form and in substance, with Section 17” of the committee rules.

Pursuant to Section 18(C) of the rules, the committee formally transmitted the complaint to Dela Rosa and invited him to provide “any information relevant to the complaint, including a written response, within fifteen (15) days from receipt of this notice.”
The complaint was originally filed on Feb. 25, 2026 and the committee informed Dela Rosa of the filing on April 28.
On May 4, the panel returned the complaint to the complainants for failure to substantially comply with Section 17 of the rules, prompting the group to file supplemental affidavits on Sept. 14.

articles.title: PAL firms up first Dreamliner order
articles.summary: Flag carrier Philippine Airlines is adding up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners to its fleet, as it maximizes its international network for future growth.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
Planes land and take off at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Pasay City on March 23, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — Flag carrier Philippine Airlines is adding up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners to its fleet, as it maximizes its international network for future growth.
In a signing, PAL entered into agreements with aerospace giant Boeing to buy 15 Dreamliners as was announced during the Farnborough International Airshow in July.
The agreements also cover the opportunity to purchase another five in the future, providing PAL with the flexibility to broaden its fleet as demand requires.
The 787-10, the largest member of the Dreamliner family, aims to boost PAL’s fleet upgrade. The aircraft will enable PAL to raise capacity for medium- and long-range flight.
Boeing committed to deliver the Dreamliner to PAL over the next decade. PAL will also become the first domestic carrier with a Dreamliner in its fleet, marking a new era for Philippine aviation.
PAL Holdings Inc. president and chief operating officer Lucio Tan III said the Dreamliner would enhance the airline’s fuel efficiency, given that the aircraft is equipped with new technologies.
“Its advanced technology, greater passenger capacity and improved fuel efficiency will also help us serve more passengers, improve our product offering and operate more efficiently,” Tan said.
The Dreamliner that PAL ordered would be powered by GE Aerospace’s GEnx-1B engines, one of the aviation industry’s most reliable mechanisms right now.
The Dreamliner is arguably the industry’s most popular aircraft because of its features. For one, the unit is the lightest and smoothest widebody jet, making long-range flights more comfortable.

Further, the 787-10 that PAL ordered is the biggest variant of the Dreamliner family, capable of flying between 300 and 375 passengers. The aircraft can fly as far as 13,890 kilometers and for PAL, this means reaching destinations across the Pacific Ocean.
Boeing also flexes the sustainability advantage of the Dreamliner, as it burns 25 percent less fuel compared to previous generations.
For passengers, the Dreamliner brings better comfort in its dimmable windows, higher humidity for dry air and reduced noise during turbulence.

articles.title: President Marcos, Chinese foreign minister discuss West Philippine Sea issues
articles.summary: President Marcos is hopeful for “better” and “improved” relations with China, following his recent conversation with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Shenzhen, China.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arrives in a vehicle at the Philippine International Convention Center for the opening ceremonies of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Meetings in Manila on November 15, 2026.
AFP / Rolex Dela Pena / Pool
MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos is hopeful for “better” and “improved” relations with China, following his recent conversation with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Shenzhen, China.
Marcos said while he didn’t get the chance to speak with Chinese President Xi Jinping, he had a “long conversation” with Wang on several matters, including the West Philippine Sea.

“As you can imagine, it’s very difficult to have any kind of extended interaction with President Xi, because he’s also very, very busy,” the President told the Philippine media delegation who covered his participation in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders’ meeting and related activities yesterday.

“I had an opportunity during the gala dinner, quite by coincidence, or maybe by design, I don’t know, to sit next to Foreign Minister Wang Yi. And over dinner we had a long conversation on several matters,” he said.
According to Marcos, he discussed with Wang “how we can move together, how we can lower tensions in the West Philippine Sea, how we can deal with each other in a better way.”
Marcos said he is “very optimistic” that the Philippines and China will “find better ways to deal with the difficulties that we have.”

“I think, because Foreign Minister Wang Yi and I were able to speak, even though I wasn’t able to talk to President Xi, we were able to discuss a lot of things that I think will be for the better,” he said, emphasizing the two countries’ trade and investment relations.
China, Asean want COC – BBM
Meanwhile, Marcos said China and all member-states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are supportive of finalizing a code of conduct (COC) in the South China Sea.
“All the ASEAN leadership would like a COC. And I think, I feel it very strongly that China would also like to have a COC. And they say so,” Marcos said.
He credited the support and cooperation of the Chinese on the progress of finalizing the COC.

Marcos said Singapore, the next chair of the ASEAN, now holds the initiative to move things forward for the finalization of the COC, which seeks to establish rules for managing maritime disputes and preventing confrontations in the South China Sea.
“I’m highly encouraged by the attitude that they bring to those negotiations. And let’s really hope that Singapore will be able to host the actual finalization of the COC,” Marcos said.
At a press conference after the closing ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Pasay City on Tuesday, Marcos said the major issues surrounding the proposed rules have been settled.

articles.title: Impeachment court issues show-cause order to VP spokesman
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court on Friday issued a show-cause order to Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo over statements that allegedly cast doubt on the integrity of…

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court on Friday issued a show-cause order to Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo over statements that allegedly cast doubt on the integrity of senator-judges.

The order, which carries a potential contempt citation, was approved at the start of Day 45 of Duterte’s impeachment trial following a formal motion by Sen. Erwin Tulfo. No senator-judge raised an objection.
Tulfo flagged Panelo’s public remarks, arguing that the spokesman disrespected the tribunal by commenting on the senators while his principal is on trial.

“He’s not party to this case, but he is the spokesperson of the Vice President. I mean, you are the spokesperson of the Vice President that is on trial here, and then you would comment on the senator-judges, the impeachment court. It seems there is no respect for the impeachment court,” Tulfo said at the trial on Friday.
In response, Panelo maintained that his comments “were fair, made in good faith.”
“I will formally respond to the show-cause order within the period provided upon receipt,” Panelo said in a statement. — Bella Cariaso, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: ‘Cale88 Foods named after VP spouse, dentist’
articles.summary: Cale88 Foods Corp., the banana chips exporter co-owned by Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio and her dentist Lourdes Lebosada, takes its name from the first two letters of…
articles.byline: Daphne Galvez, Bella Cariaso, Neil Jayson Servallos

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Cale88 Foods Corp., the banana chips exporter co-owned by Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio and her dentist Lourdes Lebosada, takes its name from the first two letters of their surnames paired with a number symbolizing infinity, a trade official confirmed to the Senate impeachment court on Friday.

Testifying as a defense witness, Department of Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo clarified the origin and pronunciation of the company’s name after presiding officer Francis Escudero asked whether it is pronounced with two syllables.
“When we asked the Davao BOI extension office, they said that in the ‘kah-leh’ the CA was the surname (of Carpio) while the LE was Lebosada, so ‘kah-leh,’” Rodolfo told the court.
“For Cale88, the eight was for infinity, so Cale88,” he added, referring to the number traditionally regarded as lucky.
“So, Cale88 was the pronunciation. So, at least we’re pronouncing it correctly,” Escudero replied.
Carpio and Lebosada each hold a 47.5 percent stake in Cale88, which is listed as a business interest of the Vice President’s husband.

The firm has drawn scrutiny during Duterte’s impeachment trial after Sen. Risa Hontiveros flagged its foreign remittances – including funds from Chinese entities and a Ukrainian company facing criminal complaints for money laundering and fraud.

Financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera also previously testified that Cale88’s financial statements lacked reported accounts receivable, accounts payable and raw material inventory, despite substantial cash inflows and outflows.

The Anti-Money Laundering Council had earlier reported that the firm grossed more than P1 billion at one point and it received P776 million in foreign remittances from 2022 to 2025, including P319 million from China.
Zero employees
Rodolfo confirmed that Cale88 Foods Corp. had no employees in 2024 and only two employees in 2025.
The vice chairman and managing head of the Board of Investments made the confirmation during the cross-examination of counsel for the prosecution Erwin Matib.

Rodolfo was confronted with the general information sheet submitted by Cale88 to the BOI. Based on the document, Rodolfo said Cale88 reported three officers, zero rank-and-file employees and zero manpower complement in 2024.

Meanwhile, for 2025, the firm had two officers, two employees and no manpower complement. Rodolfo said he did not see any submission by Cale88 on its employees’ Social Security System and PhilHealth benefits.
FDA registration
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a certificate of product registration to Calle88 Food Corp. for sweetened banana chips on Aug. 17, 2022, valid until Aug. 16, 2027.

Defense counsel Justin Nicol Gular presented FDA Center for Food Regulation and Research director Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan to prove Calle88 was in the lawful legitimate export business of sweetened banana chips and had the requisite license to operate and certificate of product registration.
Pagayunan said the FDA initially rejected the application of Calle88.

“This was the packaging that was submitted in the initial application and it was evaluated in accordance to the regulations of the FDA on food labeling. That’s why there was a denial as a result of that initial evaluation,” she said.
Labor complaint
Cale88 may face a separate labor complaint after company records suggested its workers earned only about P75 a day, the House prosecution panel said.
Panel spokesman Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong questioned payroll figures submitted to BOI showing that Cale88 had 115 workers but spent only P3.112 million on their annual compensation.

Based on those figures, he said each worker would have received an average of P27,061 a year, or about P2,255 a month, assuming the payroll was divided equally among employees working throughout the year.

articles.title: Fuel prices going down by P2/liter
articles.summary: A rollback of at least P2 per liter is looming at the pumps next week, potentially marking the third straight round of price cuts, even as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
A gas station attendant fills up cars at a station in Paco, Manila on January 12, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Edd Gumban
MANILA, Philippines — A rollback of at least P2 per liter is looming at the pumps next week, potentially marking the third straight round of price cuts, even as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.
Early industry estimates point to a reduction of P2.35 to P2.55 per liter for diesel and P2 to P2.15 per liter for gasoline.
The projected adjustments are based on the four-day trading in the regional benchmark Mean of Platts Singapore, although they have yet to account for freight and insurance costs.
Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said oil prices declined this week due to growing expectations of a supply surplus, coupled with a weaker demand outlook.
The continued slide in prices comes despite fading hopes of an imminent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route whose closure has fueled concerns over supply disruptions.

“Increasing supply from the Middle East through alternative routes continue to weigh on the market, although risks are still being priced in as attacks on shipping and Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure continue, and the US blockade on Iran remains,” Bellas said.

While the Philippines sources most of its refined petroleum products like gasoline and diesel from other Asian countries, refineries in these markets remain heavily reliant on crude oil imports from the Middle East.

articles.title: Bring in ‘cosmetic cowboys’ law to avoid more deaths, says family of butt lift victim
articles.summary:
Relatives speak out as inquest jury find Alice Webb’s death after filler entered her organs was accidental

The family of a woman who died after a botched Brazilian butt lift have called for…

blocks.text: The family of a woman who died after a botched Brazilian butt lift have called for laws against “cosmetic cowboys” to be introduced before more people lose their lives.
Speaking as an inquest jury concluded Alice Webb’s death was accidental, her family said they were astonished people were still having BBLs despite what had happened to her.
Webb, 33, collapsed and died after undergoing a BBL by Jordan Parke, known as the “Lip King”, at a treatment room in Gloucestershire.
Jurors were told Parke injected Webb with seven times the amount of filler he had been taught to use, and a postmortem found traces of the gel-like substance in her heart, lung, kidneys and brain.

blocks.caption: Jordan Parke, pictured on the This Morning TV programme in 2015, died this year. Photograph: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The procedure took place in a small treatment room in a semi-detached house which did not have equipment such as ultrasound probes to help a practitioner ensure they were injecting the correct layer of skin. There was no life-saving kit on hand.

Speaking outside the Gloucestershire coroner’s court, Webb’s family said they wanted an “Alice’s law” to be brought in as soon as possible. April Palmer, Webb’s sister, said: “We’d like to see tighter regulation, more protection.”
She said it was astounding that people were still having BBLs. “We need the government to take urgent action. We believe it could prevent avoidable harm and spare other families the same heartbreak.”

blocks.caption: Alice Webb’s sister, April Palmer, and her former partner, Ben Kingscote, outside the coroner’s court during the inquest.

blocks.text: Palmer said her sister had struggled with “low self-worth” and subjected herself to cosmetic procedures as she sought “elusive perfection”.
Last month, the UK government announced what it billed a “cosmetic cowboys crackdown” for England that includes only allowing doctors to carry out BBLs. It is currently consulting on its plans.

Ben Kingscote, Webb’s former partner and the father of the eldest of her three children, said: “The government has announced these regulations but they haven’t implemented them. They need to get on with it, get it done.”

During the inquest the jury heard Parke had been banned from carrying out BBLs in two areas of England because of his unsafe practices, but had been able to work elsewhere. Kingscote said: “We want to see prohibition orders recognised nationally rather than locally.”

Ashton Collins, the director of Save Face, a register of aesthetic practitioners, said it had taken too long for the proposed law changes to be drafted. She expressed concern there would be a rise in the number of people trying to get BBLs and other procedures before any changes came into effect.
after newsletter promotion
“We are seeing a huge rise in adverts from unscrupulous and unsafe providers offering Black Friday and Christmas special offers,” Collins said.

During the inquest, jurors were told the filler may have got into Webb’s system when a blood vessel was damaged during the BBL. In her final messages to family as she underwent the treatment, Webb said she was in pain, writing: “OMG – it kills.”

Police said they had found many other people who had suffered after treatment by Parke and were confident they would have brought a case of gross negligence manslaughter against him, but he died earlier this year.
The jury said in its findings that Webb died from “complications arising from BBL procedure”.
The senior coroner Katy Skerrett said she would be writing a “preventing future deaths report” detailing her concerns about the lack of regulation in the aesthetics industry.

A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Social Care said: “The government is already taking strict action to protect people from rogue operators. We have set out tough new proposals to restrict liquid Brazilian butt lifts and other body filler procedures to doctors, while ensuring other high-risk cosmetic procedures can only be carried out by appropriately qualified healthcare professionals.

“Those who break the rules risk criminal enforcement and unlimited fines. We are pressing ahead with these reforms, with draft regulations already out for consultation and the required period of parliamentary scrutiny scheduled for spring 2027.”

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones' daughter says parents warned her about 'nepo baby' label
articles.summary: Carys Douglas, 23, made her stage debut this year in Anton Chekhov's play, The Seagull, in the US.

blocks.text: Catherine Zeta-Jones's daughter has said her parents warned her people might have "preconceived notions" about her embarking on an acting career, as she shared her views on the "nepo baby" label.
Carys Douglas, 23, made her stage debut this year, playing the lead role of Nina in Anton Chekhov's The Seagull in Brooklyn, New York.

Zeta-Jones who is married to Michael Douglas, son of Hollywood star Kirk, previously said the "nepo baby" term was "horrific". It refers to children of famous parents perceived to have achieved riches and success off their parents' backs.
But the young actor said her parents taught her to build her "own identity" and that she has learned how to deal with the "pressure".
During an interview with Elle Spain, Carys Douglas said her parents "do not hide" from her that people would have preconceived ideas about her.
"They taught me that building my own identity depended on me and no one else. It was my responsibility, and it still is.
"As time has gone on, I've come to understand that there are different ways to deal with that kind of pressure," she said.
Her father, star of hit 1980s films such as Wall Street and Fatal Attraction, recently stated that he is not a fan of the "nepo baby" label, calling it an "unfortunate title".

"I guess you could say that about any business. The same thing with Hollywood royalty. My father's father was a junkman," Douglas, 82, said, referring to Kirk, who was considered a Hollywood Golden Age icon.
Zeta-Jones, 57, from Mumbles, Swansea, also criticised the phrase, saying it was "horrible because these kids didn't ask to be born into this, they're finding their own way in life".
"You have to go with your dreams, your passion," Zeta-Jones said.
She added: "But they love it, and they're good. Otherwise, Michael and I would be the first to go, 'you know what? Maybe law school looks really good'."
Zeta-Jones' big break came when she landed a West End role in 42nd Street in 1987, before she became a household name in the UK in 1991 after starring in the ITV hit The Darling Buds Of May.
She has since become a global superstar, with roles in The Mask Of Zorro, Entrapment, Traffic and 2002's adaptation of Chicago, for which she won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress.
The couple's children, Dylan and Carys, have both followed in their footsteps into acting.
Michael Douglas said his children have been performing "since they were in kindergarten".
"Every play, every show, summer theater camps, graduating... I mean, they've done so much work. It's unbelievable," he said.
Douglas and Zeta-Jones' children predominantly grew up in the US, but the family regularly travels to Wales, a place they are fond of.
Speaking to British Vogue last November, Carys Douglas said her summers were spent reading on her grandmother's sofa and travelling around the Gower Peninsula in Swansea.
"I feel so lucky that this is where I'm from," she told the magazine, reflecting on the "weird but magical places" scattered across the peninsula.
"Those beaches are some of the most beautiful in the world," she said.
"The Gower Peninsula is breathtaking."
She also spoke about her "theatrical" family's traditions, recalling how "there'd be lots of little competitions for singing and pantomime shows all summer".
"It's true, the Welsh love to sing," she added.

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 45: Cale88 seen as small-time despite millions in money flows
articles.summary: The 45th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte began with the Senate impeachment court ordering OVP spokesperson Paolo Panelo to explain his remarks alleging bias by some…

blocks.text: The 45th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte began with the Senate impeachment court ordering OVP spokesperson Paolo Panelo to explain his remarks alleging bias by some senator-judges.
Panelo defended his comments as part of his freedom of speech.

Defense witness and Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo testified that Cale88 Foods Corp., a listed business interest of the Vice President’s husband, Manases Carpio, is a registered micro, small and medium enterprise.
Likewise, Rodolfo said the firm stopped operations in 2025 due to a change in ownership.
Rodolfo also said that, from 201 employees in 2024, the firm only had 50 workers in 2025 based on its submissions to the Board of Investments under DTI.

At the same time, Rodolfo testified that Cale88 only had zero and two employees in 2024 and 2025, respectively, based on the firm’s General Information Sheet submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The witness said there was no reason for Cale88 Foods Corporation to surpass its declared sales of P208 million in 2022 to 2025.

He made the testimony after senator-judges pointed out that the money inflow and outflow to Cale88 accounts reached P1.2 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions based on the records of the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said it was puzzling that Cale88 did not apply for incentives when it registered before the BOI, which regulates fiscal incentives for firms and considering the billions worth of bank transactions that it recorded under its account.
Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros said it "sounds bananas" that Cale88 was able to produce 422,000 kilos of banana chips in 2025 with only two employees and three officials.

Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Director Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan, meanwhile, testified that Cale88 Foods Corp. was granted product registration documents, or the Certificate of Product Registration.
The FDA official, however, said she won’t be able to testify on the capacity of Cale88 to produce over 400,000 kilos of banana chips.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero asked the defense team if they bought a sample of the banana chips.
Defense counsel Justin Gular, however, said the defense does not have samples of the chips.
Gular said they will present a proper witness who can speak on Cale88’s production.
The impeachment trial will resume on December 1 to give way to the ongoing Senate deliberations on the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: US army postpones plan to detonate bomb-making chemical amid outcry
articles.summary:
Controlled detonation could lead to plume containing lead particles, worrying residents and state officials

The US army has delayed…

blocks.text: The US army has delayed its plan to detonate a stash of bomb-making chemicals in south-eastern Iowa after an outpouring of public concern that a cloud of lead dust could cause environmental contamination and health problems.
The plan is now to carry it out on Monday.

Kim Reynolds, the governor of Iowa, who was among those who called for the detonation to be delayed as the clock ticked down Thursday, spoke directly with Adam Telle, acting secretary of the army, her office said. Environmental groups filed a lawsuit earlier in the day, seeking emergency court action to halt the plan.
The army was initially set to blow up about 5 tons of lead azide in Middletown, Iowa, at noon on Friday, a move it described as the safest way to dispose of the highly sensitive compound.

Planning for the detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant began after staff earlier this year found several dozen barrels containing lead azide that had degraded, “creating a highly unstable and dangerous situation,” according to an emergency permit approved last week by the US Environmental Protection Agency. Moving or relocating it posed an unacceptable risk of accidental detonation, a possibility that increases in cold weather.

“This will delay the detonation until the latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material,” Telle said in a post on X announcing the push to Monday.
During the controlled explosion, barrels of the material would be stored inside concrete structures and surrounded by sand-filled Hesco barriers reaching up two storeys high.

Army officials advised certain residents of Middletown to evacuate between 8am and 2pm local time, due to the potential for window damage. The vibrations from the two blasts would not last long but could break old windows in town, and the resulting dust was expected to linger for no more than one hour, depending on wind speed, officials said.
The detonation was also expected to produce a plume containing lead particles.

Officials have released maps showing the potential for lead dust to drift north. Updated maps showed the plume’s shift, and the army will continue to update the map based on weather. Some schools in the path of the plume have already canceled classes.
Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but there are thousands more in the path of the plume.
While the army recommends cleaning cars, windowsills and outdoor surfaces after the detonation, residents have taken to social media to voice concern and question whether that will be enough.
Iowa’s top leaders appeared to learn about the plan along with the public. Reynolds was first briefed on Monday about the public advisory, her office said.

“An unacceptable lack of communication and clarity has made Iowans understandably concerned and angry about this situation,” Rob Sand, the governor elect, wrote on X on Thursday. “The public deserves to know, if this is the safest option, why other options were worse.”
Telle alluded to the criticism in his Thursday announcement about the delayed detonation.
“Public communication is essential to public trust,” he wrote on X, adding that he was engaging state officials.
Describing the new plan to proceed on MondayTelle said it is the “latest possible moment”, before temperatures drop, which could risk destabilizing the material.

Middletown residents learned in March that the army needed to dispose of several dozen barrels containing lead azide, after the ammunition plant paused operations as part of a review and the degraded material was discovered.

“The safety of our people and our neighbors is non‑negotiable,” Lt Col Daniel Nosse, the commander of the plant, said at the time, acknowledging the volatility of the chemical compound used in munitions production.

The army shared more details during a public meeting in Middletown in October, advising that a detonation was planned for an unspecified date in November. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) on 13 November approved an emergency permit, paving the way for Friday’s detonation.

That permit required the army to track specific rates of potential air and dust dispersion and notify the public five days in advance, prompting Sunday’s original advisory to communities as far as 100 miles (160km) away.

Just a few miles north-west, the Danville community school district will close on Friday, the superintendent said in an announcement on Tuesday. Pat Wallace said his initial intention was to keep schools open, but there were enough uncertainties that made canceling “the most responsible decision”.
Many schools throughout the region had already announced closures Friday and would now have to decide how to proceed on Monday.

Lucy Giehl, her husband and two dogs live just about four miles (6.4km) north of the ammunition plant. She first learned of the detonation on Sunday and was still trying to figure out where she’d go during the detonation.

But Giehl, 64, also wondered what happens when she gets home after. She voiced frustration about the lack of information about how to mitigate the risks. Her questions remained Thursday even after the delay.

“What are they going to do during those three days to help people be better prepared?” Giehl asked, asking whether she needs to wear gloves to wipe down surfaces or to keep her dogs from drinking water in their pond. “There’s just so many details that I feel like haven’t been addressed with the public.”

Environmental groups sued Thursday in an effort to stop the detonation, arguing that the EPA failed to require the Army to consider safer alternatives and that the Army failed to give adequate notice of its plans.
The detonation should be canceled outright, not merely delayed, said Wally Taylor, legal chair for the Sierra Club, one of the groups involved in the lawsuit.
“We don’t want the explosion to take place at all,” Taylor said Thursday after the announcement. “There are ways to do it without all the air quality problems and potential health problems.”

Patrick O’Shaughnessy, a professor at the University of Iowa’s department of occupational and environmental health, said it was encouraging to see that the army and the EPA were doing all they could to minimize the dust, but it was still unknown how much would end up in the atmosphere and on surfaces.

Lead is a neurological toxicant that can decrease brain activity and development, especially in young children, O’Shaughnessy said. He is particularly concerned for toddlers who are at the age of putting everything in their mouth.

According to EPA documents, alternatives such as neutralizing and decomposing the contents of the drums using other chemicals were considered. But officials said any plan that involved handling the drums would increase the probability of accidental, fatal detonation.

Iowa State’s Des Moines county extension field office was busy taking calls Thursday from concerned residents who have been “deathly afraid” for their health and their animals, said staff member Morgan Hoenig.
“We ran out of soil test kits yesterday,” she said.

articles.title: AFP eyes kinetic weapons to boost territorial defense
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is eyeing the acquisition of kinetic weapon systems to strengthen the country's territorial defense and protect its sea lanes.

blocks.text: Published November 20, 2026 11:28pm
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is eyeing the acquisition of kinetic weapon systems to strengthen the country's territorial defense and protect its sea lanes.

In a report by Chino Gaston on "24 Oras" on Friday, US President Donald Trump announced a $2-billion military loan for the Philippines during his visit to the country, equivalent to around P127 billion.
Of this amount, $400 million will be allocated to strengthening the military's capabilities to deter potential attacks in the West Philippine Sea.
One of the capabilities being considered involves kinetic weapons, which can strike targets at long range on land or at sea.
These weapons use the kinetic energy generated by the speed and mass of a projectile, such as missiles and bullets, to hit their targets.

"These are weapon systems which have larger range. So, there are missile systems. The missile systems will not be effective if there is no radar. Of course, you need to detect where the threat is," Major General Oliver Maquiling, director of the AFP's DAGITPA Exercise, said in a mix of English and Filipino.
AFP Chief of Staff General Antonio Nafarrete said these weapons are important in deterring foreign vessels from entering the country's sea lanes.

"We concentrate now on kinetic requirements basically for territorial defense talaga, ensuring pag may mga… kasi ito archipelagic. Pumapasok na yung mga PLA (People's Liberation Army) na mga naval vessels dito sa sea lines of communication natin. That’s international kasi, so we must have that deterrent capability," Nafarette said.

(We are now focusing on kinetic requirements, primarily for territorial defense. Given that the Philippines is an archipelagic country and Chinese naval vessels are entering our sea lines of communication, we must have that deterrent capability.)
The deployment and use of missile systems are among the capabilities being tested and practiced during the AFP's AJEX DAGITPA military exercises.
The Philippines already operates several missile systems, including the BrahMos cruise missiles acquired from India, which have a reported range of up to 300 kilometers.
The country also has C-Star anti-ship cruise missiles from South Korea. —Jean Mangaluz/VBL, GMA News

articles.title: 2 U.S. veterans, who both survived Pearl Harbor attack, die on same day
articles.summary: Two former U.S service members who were stationed at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii when Japan attacked in 1941 died on the same day last week, it has been learned.

image.caption: Geb Galle speaks with reporters before a commemoration ceremony at the USS Nevada Memorial on Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam on the island of Oahu, Hawaii, on Dec. 8, 2016. Galle survived the 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor and died last week in Washington state. (Petty Officer 2nd Class Jared E. Walker

blocks.text: Two former U.S service members who were stationed at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii when Japan attacked in 1941 died on the same day last week, it has been learned.
Gebhard (Geb) Galle, died on Saturday at his home in Moses Lake, Wash., according to his daughter, Lynda Palmer. He was 105.
Galle died the same day as the oldest known Pearl Harbor survivor, Freeman Johnson, of Centerville, Mass., who was 106.
Galle and Johnson were among the estimated 87,000 military personnel on Oahu on Dec. 7, 1941, when Japan attacked — killing just over 2,400 Americans and drawing the U.S. into the Second World War.
The list of surviving veterans from the attack had stood at about a dozen names since the December 2025 death of Ira (Ike) Schab, who was 105.
The American Legion commended Galle and Johnson as "two members of a generation whose courage and sacrifice will forever be part of our nation's history," in a post on X.
Galle was serving aboard the battleship USS Nevada, while Freeman was with the cruiser USS St. Louis at the time of the attack, the veterans' organization noted.
Freeman Johnson looks down at his navy cap during an interview at his home in Centerville, Mass., on May 6. (Charles Krupa/The Associated Press)
Galle was born in Germany. He came to North Dakota with his family as a child and joined the U.S. navy in 1939 at age 18.
He was a machinist's mate aboard the Nevada, and was waiting below deck to be taken ashore for church services on Dec. 7, 1941. He looked out of a porthole and saw planes approaching.

A torpedo struck the ship, allowing water to enter, but officers were able to get it moving, the navy said. The ship was attacked again, causing more leaks in the hull and fires. The Nevada ran aground.
Galle could not see what was happening.
"Of course, we felt a couple jolts, and that's when we got hit with the torpedo, and we had a few bomb hits," he told the Columbia Basin Herald, a newspaper based in Moses Lake, in 2020.
LISTEN | FDR promises 'absolute victory' in historic address:
Archives7:20Japanese bomb Pearl Harbor: 'A date which will live in infamy'
"After we were beached and everything, and we got up to topside, then we saw all the mess that took place," including the capsized USS Oklahoma and the partially submerged USS Arizona, he said.
"A pretty sad lookout," Galle said.
Another near-death experience
Galle was reassigned to the USS Northampton. That ship came under fire on Nov. 30, 1942, by Japanese torpedoes during the Battle of Tassafaronga.

Galle told the Basin Herald he was ordered to leave a hatch closed behind four sailors who would've been trapped when the ship was sinking. The officer left, but Galle defied the order, opening the hatch. He closed and secured it after the sailors escaped.

"He heard those guys pounding on the roof of the hatch," Palmer said. "He went to open it up, and the senior officer walked by and said, 'No, leave it closed, because we don't want water to get in there because the ship might go down.'"
The Northampton sank, and Galle and other sailors spent more than a day adrift in life rafts before they were rescued.
Canadians mark Remembrance Day across the country

His "courage under fire" in that incident, as well as his having fought in 19 of 20 Pacific naval engagements, was noted in a 2025 letter from then-acting Chief of Naval Operations Adm. James Kilby, marking Galle's 104th birthday.
"Your humility, quick thinking and selfless actions remain a shining example of Navy valour," Kilby wrote.

In December 2016, Galle attended a 75th anniversary service at Pearl Harbor to honour and commemorate the USS Nevada and those who served on it. A total of 76 sailors and marines lost their lives as a result of that attack, the navy said.

After the war, Galle got married and opened a refrigeration and air-conditioning business in Grafton, N.D. He then served as a civil engineer with the air force and then later worked for the Army Corps of Engineers. He retired in the 1980s.
Johnson's death was confirmed by one of his daughters, Diane Johnson.

An explosion erupts at the Naval Air Station on Ford Island, as the USS Shaw explodes in the centre background during the 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor. The USS Nevada is also visible in the middle background, with its bow headed toward the left. (Fox Photos/Getty Images)

Johnson was working on a boiler of the USS St. Louis when the Japanese surprise attack occurred. In a May 2026 interview with The Associated Press, Johnson said he didn't hear or see the attack. He never heard his shipmates firing anti-aircraft guns at the attacking planes.
"While all the rigamarole was going on topside, I was inside a steam drum. Couldn't see anything, absolutely nothing," said Johnson.

items: Descendants say reviving Japanese Canadian veterans' Legion rights historical wrong
Trump to Japan's PM: 'Why didn’t you tell me about Pearl Harbor?'

blocks.text: While Johnson didn't see the Pearl Harbor attack, he was witness to other historic moments during the war.

He helped commission the USS Iowa and recalled the battleship's preparations in November 1943 ahead of transporting President Franklin D. Roosevelt to the Tehran Conference with British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Josef Stalin.
He also witnessed the war's end while aboard the Iowa. He was on its mast on Sept. 2, 1945, watching the surrender ceremonies about a mile away on the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay.
"I could see the boats coming up with the marines escorting the Japanese onto the ship and sitting around a table," he said. "It was all over."

We say goodbye to another one of our treasured heroes! Freeman Johnson, one of the oldest remaining survivors of the attack on Pearl Harbor, has died at the age of 106. Johnson passed away on November 14, 2026 at his home in Centerville, Massachusetts. On December 7, 1941, he was among an estimated 87,000 military personnel stationed on Oahu when Japan launched its surprise attack on Pearl Harbor. Serving aboard the USS St. Louis, Johnson was working below deck on a boiler when the attack began. He later recalled that he heard and saw none of the chaos unfolding above him. “While all the rigamarole was going on topside, I was inside a steam drum. Couldn’t see anything, absolutely nothing,” he told The Associated Press in a May 2026 interview. His remarkable military career continued beyond Pearl Harbor. Johnson helped commission the USS Iowa, served aboard the battleship during its preparations to transport President Franklin D. Roosevelt to the 1943 Tehran Conference, and witnessed one of history’s defining moments: Japan’s formal surrender aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945. From the attack on Pearl Harbor to the end of World War II, Freeman Johnson lived through a pivotal chapter in American history. Rest in peace, Sir! We thank you for your service! #WeRememberThem—WWIIMemorial
For all the attention to Pearl Harbor, the gruff Johnson, who was known for his cackling laugh and mischievous smile, didn't see it as one of the defining moments in his life.

Those would have been getting married after the war to his late wife and having three daughters. He worked for years in a machinist shop, then in a convenience store and, finally, delivering meals to seniors. He finally retired from all work at age 90.

articles.title: Young people across Europe stage coordinated ‘fight for our future’ protests
articles.summary:
Activists in more than 20 countries demonstrate over cost of living, learning conditions and rising military spending

Students and young workers have taken to the streets in more than 20…

blocks.text: Students and young workers have taken to the streets in more than 20 European countries in coordinated protests over the surging cost of living and housing, deteriorating learning conditions and rising military spending.

Activists from more than 50 groups in countries including Belgium, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Portugal, Spain and the UK held rallies on Friday, lighting flares, burning cardboard models of tanks and waving placards, many reading “fight for our future”.

Calling it Europe’s biggest coordinated youth protest of recent years, the Youth Strike coalition said demonstrations were planned in about 400 cities under a common slogan, “fight for our future, not their wars”.

It made five broad demands, including an end to militarisation and conscription; structural investment in education and welfare; solidarity with Palestine; climate and social justice, and a “radical transformation of the system we live in”.

An Italian organiser, Alessandro di Miceli, said the Europe-wide protests were “to claim our right to a better and dignified future”. Specific demands differed from country to country, he said, but were all “deeply connected between each other”.

A Portuguese organiser, Leonor Chicó, said: “As young people, we know that we must organise and fight for our future, because no one else will do it for us.” Governments “show us every day that the needs of our generation are not their priority”, she said.

blocks.caption: Students rally in Lisbon on Friday. Photograph: Miguel A Lopes/EPA

blocks.text: Shabbir Lakha from the UK-based Stop The War coalition said the mobilisation was “a crucial step towards building a lasting international movement capable of bringing together young people, students and workers around common demands”.

After weeks of demonstrations across several countries sparked by long-running French school protests, governments are struggling to respond to growing calls for affordable housing, functioning public services and greater social equality.

Among the organisers of Friday’s rallies in France were the gilets jaunes (yellow vests), whose protests rocked the country in 2018 and 2019, while in Germany, about 1,000 students demonstrated in Berlin over fears of a return to compulsory military service.

In Rome, Milan and other Italian cities, tens of thousands protested as the country’s largest trade union, the CGIL, ⁠staged a general strike against ⁠the economic policies of the prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, which it described as the country’s call for change.
after newsletter promotion

“We ​are living under a government that is cutting healthcare and education, taking away our present and trying to rob us of our future,” said Laura Peritore, 24, a university student. “We will not back down and will take our future back.”

At a youth-led demonstration in London, marchers waved banners reading: “No to war, racism, climate crisis, capitalism.” In Spain, the protests fell on the anniversary of the death of the late dictator Francisco Franco.
Agence France-Presse and Reuters contributed reporting
